claims.text: A critical grain size of approximately 30 nm governs a transition in the sliding response of HEA coatings.
Below the critical grain size, sliding produces an ultra-nanocrystalline or amorphous near-surface layer.
Formation of the refined or amorphous surface layer lowers shear strength through inverse Hall–Petch behavior.
The dynamically formed near-surface layer reduces friction and wear.
A coarse-grained CoCrFeMnNi coating with grains larger than 30 nm does not undergo dynamic amorphization during wear.
Processing changes such as cooling-rate or milling-time variation can produce coatings spanning both sides of the proposed 30 nm threshold.
An inert or ultra-high-vacuum environment minimizes oxidation and mixed metal-oxide film formation.
The wear-induced surface-layer transition is triggered by the coating's pre-test bulk grain size being below the critical threshold.
Below approximately 30 nm, dislocation-mediated plasticity is suppressed.
Below approximately 30 nm, grain-boundary sliding becomes the dominant deformation mode.
Surface-localized shear-induced severe plastic deformation can cause dynamic softening in the inverse Hall–Petch regime.
Coatings with initial grain sizes below 30 nm will have lower friction coefficients than otherwise comparable coatings with larger grains.
Coatings with initial grain sizes below 30 nm will have lower specific wear rates than otherwise comparable coatings with larger grains.
CoCrFeMnNi can exhibit inverse Hall–Petch behavior and a low friction coefficient of approximately 0.3 in ultra-high vacuum.
Initially coarse-grained CoCrFeMnNi can have a wear rate of approximately 10^-6 mm3/N-m in an inert environment.
The proposed mechanism should hold during dry sliding in inert environments and at moderate temperatures where oxidation is minimal.
Changing alloy chemistry or using extreme test temperatures may shift the critical grain size or change the mechanism.
Failure of sub-30-nm coatings to form the proposed surface layer would falsify the hypothesis.
Failure of sub-30-nm coatings to show lower friction and wear than larger-grained controls would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The baseline assumes that coarse-grained CoCrFeMnNi does not dynamically form the refined or amorphous surface layer, whereas the cited abstract reports exceptionally low wear in initially coarse-grained material and links the observed tribological performance to formation of an ultra-nanocrystalline near-surface layer.
